The integral over levels in (0,1] proves T≥D. At equality a q_z>1 would contribute additional mass above 1, and a q_z in (0,1) would cause a positive step in a level mass that must be almost everywhere constant.

For the equality set F={q_z=1}, a large multiple of the minimizing direction plus a direction excluding a second point of F excludes all outside F and that point, contradicting D=T. The a=0 case is included. If F consists only of j, strict inequalities expose j, with the singleton base already handled.
At a vertex, exposed base balance restricts every source to the single actual fiber. This yields the full ordinary one-fiber trimmed body for t<w_j and exactly the original fiber centroid for t=w_j.

At eligible nonvertices t≤D<T, distinct feasible pairs at masses 0 and T give strict ball inclusion at t. A finite supergradient at this interior t gives the prescribed support slope and the verified finite-tilt theorem yields the exact cap moments. The support indicator is unique on the fixed constraint pair.
